Get excited to join Scopely’s AI-native incubation team, which is focused on discovering the next generation of mobile games. This role can be remote in the US or hybrid in Culver City, LA.
Rather than spending years developing a single title, we believe one of the most effective ways to find great games is to rapidly transform ideas into playable experiences, launch them to real players, and learn from live market feedback.
We’re pioneering a new approach to game creation—one in which AI enables creators to work across traditional discipline boundaries, take greater ownership of ideas from concept through launch, and bring more great games to players.

If you’re passionate for rapid experimentation, enjoy navigating ambiguity, and love bringing ideas to life, you’ll feel at home on this team.
We don’t organize our work strictly around traditional disciplines. We believe AI enables skilled creators to contribute to more of the game development process than ever before. Whether your background is in engineering, design, art, or another discipline, we’re looking for people who are excited to work across boundaries, develop new skills, and use AI to turn ideas into playable games.

s.h: As an AI Game Developer, you’ll
s.t:
Own game ideas from concept through launch, helping to generate concepts and shape mechanics, player experiences, and creative direction.
Rapidly transform concepts into playable prototypes using AI-native workflows, modern game engines, and development tools.
Use AI to accelerate programming, design, art, content creation, testing, and production.
Design internal tools, automations, and agentic workflows that increase team velocity and unlock new creative possibilities.
Evaluate emerging AI technologies and experiment with new applications in game development.
Collaborate across disciplines to rapidly iterate on gameplay, features, and player experiences.
Launch prototypes to real players, analyze qualitative and quantitative feedback, and use those insights to guide future iterations.
Balance speed and quality by making thoughtful trade-offs that maximize learning.
Help define AI development practices that can scale across Scopely.
Challenge traditional game development workflows and help pioneer new approaches to creating games.

Strong expertise in at least one game development discipline, such as engineering, game design, art, technical art, or UX.
Enthusiasm for using AI to expand beyond your primary discipline and broaden your capabilities as a game creator.
Experience incorporating AI into creative or development workflows.
A preference for building, testing, and learning rather than relying on lengthy planning cycles.
Curiosity and adaptability, with an interest in learning new tools and techniques as the AI landscape evolves.
Strong product instincts and an understanding of what makes games engaging.
The ability to work effectively through ambiguity, rapid iteration, and changes in direction informed by player feedback.
Excellent communication skills and a collaborative mindset.

About Scopely
Scopely is a leading video game and global interactive entertainment company, home to many of the world’s most beloved and enduring experiences, including two of the most successful mobile games of all-time “MONOPOLY GO!” and “Pokémon GO,” along with “Stumble Guys,” “Star Trek™ Fleet Command,” “MARVEL Strike Force,” “WWE Champions,” the Scrabble® franchise, “Yahtzee® With Buddies,” and many others.

Across mobile, web, PC, and console, Scopely creates, develops, publishes, and live-operates one of the most diversified and award-winning portfolios in the games industry — bringing hundreds of millions of players together through a shared love of play.
Founded in 2011, Scopely is powered by its exceptional team — including thousands of world-class gamemakers around the globe, a distinctive tenet-driven culture, and its proprietary technology platform, Playgami.

Together, these strengths have fueled Scopely’s position as the #1 mobile games company in the U.S. and #2 globally, generating more than $10 billion in lifetime revenue.

Whether building global sensations like “MONOPOLY GO!” from the ground up, or expanding through strategic acquisitions, including the FoxNext, GSN, and Scopely Explore games businesses — Scopely consistently delivers experiences players love today and return to for years to come.
Recognized multiple times as one of the "100 Most Influential Companies in the World" by TIME magazine and one of Fast Company's "World's Most Innovative Companies" and “Best Workplaces for Innovators,” Scopely believes that video games can be a force for good — creating meaningful connections, vibrant communities, and making life better through play.
Scopely has global operations and partners across four continents in more than a dozen countries worldwide. For more information, visit: https://www.scopely.com/ .

We are seeking a Game Programmer to support technical implementation across game projects of varying scope — from small-scale productions up through AAA titles. This is an individual contributor role focused on hands-on development of gameplay systems, prototyping, and tooling within our prototype-driven environment.

Working under the direct supervision from Technical Director and alongside senior engineers, you will implement game mechanics, contribute to reusable libraries, and grow your expertise across multiple engines — primarily Unreal Engine C++, with exposure to additional platforms as projects require.

You will be supported throughout the transition from prototype to co-development or full production, receiving guidance across areas such as CI/CD, gameplay development, tooling, automation, and reusable library development.
We are especially interested in curious programmers who enjoy prototyping, experimenting with new approaches (ECS architecture, automation workflows, custom tools), and building systems that make other people's work easier. Whether you're drawn to gameplay programming, tooling, or the intersection of both — if you're eager to learn and ready to contribute from day one, we'd like to hear from you.

Technical Implementation & Prototyping
Feature Development: Implement gameplay systems and mechanics under the guidance of senior engineers, translating design concepts into functional code.
Rapid Prototyping: Build iterative prototypes to test new gameplay ideas and support project pitches, focusing on proof of concept, playability, and feel.
Library Contribution: Contribute to existing reusable technical libraries and frameworks (networking, simulation, core utilities) following established patterns. Learn to design modular, decoupled systems — such as ECS architectures — that scale cleanly across projects.
Engine Versatility: Work primarily in Unreal Engine C++, while adapting to and supporting other platforms or engines as project requirements evolve.
Tooling & Workflow Support
Developer Experience: Create and optimize internal tools and editor extensions that empower designers and artists to work more independently and efficiently.
Pipeline Support: Assist with the automation of technical workflows and CI/CD pipelines to improve build stability and deployment speed.
Systems Optimization: Identify and resolve performance bottlenecks, ensuring smooth gameplay and stability across different hardware targets.
Cross-Disciplinary Collaboration
Design Partnership: Work as a technical partner to designers and producers, providing feedback on technical feasibility and proposing practical solutions to creative challenges.
Global Coordination: Collaborate with distributed teams across different regions, ensuring technical alignment and consistent implementation of features.
Team Engagement: Share progress openly, flag blockers early, and actively participate in technical discussions to help the team find the best path forward.
Documentation: Proactively maintain clear technical notes and documentation for the systems you build to support team scaling and knowledge sharing.
Technical Growth & Quality
Engineering Practices: Adopt test-driven development (TDD) and write unit tests for critical gameplay logic, ensuring reliability and confidence in refactoring.
Continuous Learning: Proactively experiment with new patterns and industry trends to bring innovative technical solutions to the team.
Peer Review: Participate in code reviews, receiving guidance from senior engineers to improve your craft while providing constructive feedback to teammates.
Mentorship Engagement: Actively seek feedback, ask questions, and engage with the team's knowledge base to accelerate your growth as a game programmer.
Required
Strong Programming Foundation: Show good proficiency in C++ and a solid understanding of computer science fundamentals (data structures, algorithms, and memory management).
Version Control Proficiency: Comfortable working with Git or similar version control systems in collaborative environments.
Demonstrated Interest in Game Development: A portfolio of personal projects, prototypes, or contributions to existing games or mods that demonstrate your ability to turn an idea into a functional system.
Problem-Solving Mindset: Ability to break down complex technical challenges into manageable tasks and find practical, maintainable solutions.
Collaborative Spirit: Experience working with others (whether in a professional team, a game jam, or an open-source project) to achieve a shared goal.

Engine Experience: Familiarity with Unreal Engine (C++), though a strong foundation in other engines or languages is welcome.
Technical Curiosity: Interest or experience with modern architecture patterns, such as ECS, data-oriented design, or modular system architecture.
Gameplay sensitivity: Showing an understanding of what makes a game mechanic, or system engaging, intuitive, and fun is a definite plus.
Tooling Interest: Experience building custom tools, editor extensions, or automation scripts to improve development workflows.
Global Context & Language: Experience working in multicultural environments or an interest in the Japanese game development industry; Japanese language proficiency is a plus but not required.
■ Skills & Competencies
Technical Curiosity – A willingness to experiment, learn new languages and engines, and understand how things work under the hood.
Prototyping Mindset – Able to balance fast exploratory prototyping for pitches with clean, modular implementation for production.
Engineering Discipline – Appreciation for code quality, readability, and the value of test-driven development (TDD).
Debugging & Profiling – Comfortable tracking down performance bottlenecks, memory issues, and logic bugs using profiling tools and systematic debugging techniques.
Versatility – Comfortable jumping between gameplay logic, tool development, and pipeline automation.
Collaborative Communication – Able to translate technical constraints into clear information for designers and producers.

s.h: WHAT YOU WILL BE WORKING ON​
s.t:
What you will focus on
This role exists because reactive execution is no longer enough.

The OTT programming division needs a technical authority who can shift the team's positioning from "a team that delivers what it is asked to build" to "a technical partners that other studios actively seek out because of the value it brings to a game's success." That shift requires someone who can set a long-term technical vision, build scalable production ecosystems across mobile, PC, and console, and drive focused R&D including applied AI in game development, while simultaneously ensuring flawless deliveries across multiple live and co-development projects.
The real challenge is dual: you are building toward the future while keeping current production healthy. You will need to anticipate what partner studios will need before they ask, identify and close skill gaps across a team of around 35 to 40 programmers, and establish the kind of technical standards that make this studio a reference point across the organization, not just a capable executor.
What it means on a daily basis​
Monitor the technical health of multiple concurrent projects, working closely with technical leads to surface risks early, prevent bottlenecks, and keep deliveries on track.
Define and enforce studio-wide coding standards, architectural patterns, and engineering workflows, and drive their adoption across programming teams.
Lead high-impact R&D initiatives, with particular focus on AI applied to game development, and ensure successful integration of outcomes into production pipelines.
Provide hands-on technical guidance and mentoring to programmers, conducting periodic competency assessments and building clear development paths.
Act as the primary technical counterpart for co-development partner studios, aligning on architecture, tooling, style guides, and Unreal toolchain standardization across shared pipelines.
Collaborate cross-functionally with Game Design, Art, and Production to improve how programming integrates with other disciplines and contributes to overall product quality.
Strategic resource planning and project allocation in partnership with the Studio Technical Director.
What success will look like​
Within your first year, you will have made a visible and assessable impact on at least one co-development project or on a strategic technical mission defined in alignment with the studio's long-term vision. That impact will be confirmed through calibration with multiple stakeholders across the organization, not through self-assessment alone.
Who you would be working with​
You will report to the Studio Technical Director and operate across a programming department of around 35 to 40 people, spanning multiple seniority levels and allocated to live service and co-development projects on mobile, PC, and console platforms.
Your key collaborators include department heads and team leads across Game Design, Art, and Production, as well as Studio Directors and the Studio Manager. You will also work directly with Technical Managers and Technical Directors from co-development partner studios.
Your recruitment journey
Screen Call with a Recruiter
First Interview with the Studio Technical Director and Division Principal/Manager
Second Interview with Studio Manager and HR Director
Final interview with a Technical Director from a sister studio
Where this role can take you
If the opportunity arises and the qualifications are in place, this position is a direct pathway to the Studio Technical Director role. That outcome is not guaranteed, but it is a realistic evolution for the right person.
